# Researchers reality

- Knowing Git or not, must researchers reality is that manuscripts sit in DOCX and track changes
- Git stay with the coders, because the overhead was too much to ask

# Open science culture

- Open sciene is a way of working, it's not a tick box of whether or not your content is open
- Look at this figure, it's overwhelming, and doesn't cover essence
- Open science is about a culture of openessess, sharing the process of doing research, rather than end product, being transparent and making oneself vulnerable 

# Agents have made it cheap, but also insecure

- 2023: a non-forgiving terminal,  clone, branch, stage, message, push, PR text, conflicts
- 2026: say what you want, read what was done, comment on it, and integrate 
- Agents do the mechanics, Humans the important parts: validation, correction, approval 
- And with Git, all tracked and documented.
- Left to teach: reading a diff, reviewing a PR, and most importantly knowing what never enters a repository
- Not using Git made data security issues invisible, but it was never easier to paste sensitive, personal content into a chat windows, which has made data security training one of the most important aspects


# Line

> "Every PhD should be forced to learn Git" - Research Software Engineer at DSN comminuty event in Month Year

# Agreement

- I have agreed then, but would have used a different approach than force. Sadly, force might have been the only way. Luckily, that has changed now. We can finally sell it.
- Code and reproducibility is one aspect, but the reality is that this is the only record now that can tell their work from the machine's

# Complication with AI

- 30 minute papers, fake papers mined from open data
- journals asking for proof of human work, which is a step up from declaring use of AI, and a good one

# Declare vs. prove

- The current developments on AI declaration are going towards tick boxes, filled from memory. I think that's counterproductive. 
- Show screenshot of 18 boxes.
- The research papers I write, tick all boxes today. I cannot claim anymore that AI hasn't influenced my idea generation.
- Doesn't it matter more that I show my workflow, dated commits, prompts, human drafts, literature notes, compounded knowledge base (aka LLM Wiki) and am public and transparent by sharing those artifacts alongside the papers?
